docs.text: A thread of recent phone snapshots from my yard. Everything shown is native to my region (NA/Great Lakes), grown from seed, planted to replace my lawn. Binomial names in the alt text if you want to look anything up to see if it is appropriate for your garden! I'll add photos as the season goes on.

🌼 striped pipsissewa 🌿
Chimaphila maculata little evergreen plant with an unusual distribution- from indiana east to the coast, the great lakes down to central alabama & georgia... and all throughout central america from northern Mexico to Panama #nativeplants #flowerreport
Erythronium albidum or white trout lily. Taken at the heron rookery at Indiana Dunes National Park. #nativeplants #greatlakes #springeohemeral #woodlandplants
Erythronium americanum or yellow trout lily. Also photographed at the heron rookery at Indiana Dunes National Park. #nativeplants #greatlakes #springephemeral #woodlandplants

More than 30 years ago, a group of scientists planted just 4,200 seeds of the rare Pitcher’s thistle in the sandy dunes of the Great Lakes. At the time, no one knew if the populations would survive. Today, the restored populations are thriving and spreading. www.greatlakesnow.org/2026/01/02/h...
Really spectacular population of pitcher-plants (Sarracenia purpurea) in this coastal fen (I think?). Found in Thompson's Harbor State Park, along Lake Huron
I finally filled and seeded lemongrass into my Edmund Fitzgerald planter. Look at her. She’s the most gorgeous thing ever ❤️❤️ (yeaaaah Great Lakes Freighters are one of my oldest hyperfixations.)
Asclepias amplexicaulis or clasping milkweed. I don’t have a great photo of this one. Spotted at Indiana Dunes NP upland sandy soils (of course). #nativeplants #savannaplants #greatlakes

Sisyrinchium albidum or white blue-eyed grass. Well drained soils and plenty of sun make this plant happiest in meadows, glades, and openings in woodland. Spotted in N Indiana. #nativeplants #prairieplants #meadowplants #greatlakes
Hepatica acutilobia or sharp-lobed hepatica. #woodlandplants #greatlakes #nativeplants #springephemerals #spring #ephemerals

Seems like a good day for Parnassia glauca or grass of Parnassus or bog star. Found in a bog at Indiana Dunes NP. #wetlandplants #greatlakes #nativeplants #bogplants #fenplants
Cypripedium acaule or moccasin flower. From Cowels Bog Indiana Dunes National Park. Forest canopy and acidic soils. #woodlandplants #nativeplants #orchids #greatlakes

So many great species along Lake Superior this summer. One highlight was several patches of Cypripedium acaule (Pink Ladyslipper). This one was surrounded by Lysimachia borealis (Starflower) and Cornus canadensis (Candadian Bunchberry) and other great species. #nativePlants #Ontario
Houstonia caerulea or azure bluet. I can’t exactly recall where I took this photo but it’s certainly in the Great Lakes region. Likes open forests #nativeplants #foestplants #greatlakesplants

Trillium recurvatum or bloody butcher. Common in woodland understory, this photo snagged at the Heron Rookery within the Indiana Dunes National Park complex. #forestplants #greatlakes #springephemerals #nativeplants
Trillium erectum or wake-robin. This one is protected in some Great Lakes states so we’ll be keeping the location secret. #nativeplants #greatlakes #woodlandplants #springephemerals
Its the Great Lakes micro-climate keeping these plants alive and producing still.
Hepatica Americana or round-lobed hepatica. #woodlandplants #greatlakes #spring #ephemerals #springephemerals

Cirsium pitcheri or Pitcher's thistle. Native to dune ecosystems of the Great Lakes; listed as threatened. This photo snapped at Indiana Dunes National Park. #duneplants #nativeplants #greatlakesplants
Apocynum androsaemifolium or spreading dogbane. Savanna, woodland, prairie. Well drained sandy soils in Northern Indiana. #nativeplants #GreatLakes #IndianaDunes

In honour of World Wetland Day here is a photo of a badass carnivorous Purple Pitcher Plant taken at a coastal fen near the shores of Lake Huron on the Saugeen (Bruce) Peninsula. Fens are the coolest. But I could never pick a favourite wetland.
I found the federally endangered dwarf lake iris today! #botany #conservation #greatlakes
Growth of starry stonewort (Nitellopsis obtusa (Desvaux) J. Groves, Characeae) in two Michigan, USA, drowned river mouth lakes #GreatLakes 🧪 www.sciencedirect.com/science/arti...
Thank you to Great Lakes Review for republishing my musings about plants and life:) #WritingCommunity greatlakesreview.org/botanical-ga...
Trillium flexipes or declined trillium. I’ve only spotted this in ravines but that doesn’t mean it’s exclusive. Illinois Beach State Park. #nativeplants #greatlakes #springephemerals #forestplants

Geum triflorum - prairie smoke. Blooms in April. Native to the western United States and most of the Great Lakes area. Lovely pinkish red flowers with a fluffy seed head that stays on through summer. Grows and spreads slowly but surely. Plant native plants!!
Trillium grandiflorum or white trillium. Found at Indiana Dunes National Park. Prefers forest canopy cover. #woodlandplants #nativeplants #greatlakes
Behold the majesty of the native plants of the Great Lakes region
Uplift your soul with this plant revered in ancient Greece known as Dogs Tongue. Shhhhhh…this is the plant of silence 🤫. #lakemichigan #milwaukee #wisconsin #plants #flowers #naturesbeauty
The late autumn beauty of our native grass, Schizachyrium scoparium. #nativeplants #naturalgarden #gardendesigner #greatlakes #lakeontario
Beautiful plant. I saw this at Chiwaukee Prairie State Natural Area In WI, on the shores of Lake Michigan, just north of the Illinois state line.

I'm definitely still learning to ID plants, I'm not too experienced; if you are in the Eastern US this is a helpful plant key: gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org There's some species overlap into the midwest so sometimes it helps there too (I'm great lakes region so I find it relatively helpful)

In Central Algonquian (i.e. Great Lakes Algonquian), the word for "skunk", or a derivative, is also used for wild onions. In Ojibwe, "wild onion" is "ᔑᑳᑲᐧᐊᓐᔒᣖ" <zhigaag-awanzh-iig>, "skunk-plant". In Miami-Illinois, "šikaakwa" is used for both "skunk" and "wild onion"
